facts.statement: Jabalisaurus tethyensis is classified as an ophthalmosaurid ichthyosaur.
facts.quote: An ophthalmosaurid ichthyosaur; a species of Jabalisaurus.

facts.statement: The species lived during the Late Jurassic Tithonian stage.
Its type locality is the Altmühltal Formation in Germany.
The genus Jabalisaurus was established by Barrientos‑Lara and Alvarado‑Ortega in 2021.
Jabalisaurus includes two species: J. meztli and J. tethyensis.
One specimen, JME‑SOS‑08369, is a complete articulated skeleton preserved in soft tissue and had previously been identified in 2022 as Aegirosaurus sp.
facts.quote: One of these, JME-SOS-08369, is a complete, articulated skeleton encased in soft tissue. It was described previously in 2022 and identified as Aegirosaurus sp.

facts.statement: The genus Jabalisaurus is known from Late Jurassic rocks of both Mexico and Germany.
facts.quote: Jabalisaurus is an extinct genus of ophthalmosaurid ichthyosaurs known from Late Jurassic rocks of Mexico and Germany.

facts.statement: Jabalisaurus belongs to the subfamily Ophthalmosaurinae within the family Ophthalmosauridae, class Reptilia, and its known time range is the Kimmeridgian (152.21 to 149.2 million years ago).
facts.quote:
Parent group: Ophthalmosaurinae
Family: Ophthalmosauridae
Class: Reptilia
Time range: Kimmeridgian to Kimmeridgian (152.21 to 149.2 million years ago)
